messages.subject: getting replicate information
parts:
Dear all,

When a model contains a term like f(X, model = "rw1", replicate = Y) then model$summary.random has the levels of X in the ID field. But where can I find the corresponding levels of Y? Would it be possible to add them to e.g. a Replicate variable in that summary?

Best regards,

Thierry

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] getting replicate information
parts:
On Mon, 2015-11-02 at 13:46 -0800, thierry....@gmail.com wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> When a model contains a term like f(X, model = "rw1", replicate = Y)
> then model$summary.random has the levels of X in the ID field. But
> where can I find the corresponding levels of Y? Would it be possible
> to add them to e.g. a Replicate variable in that summary?

Hi,

good question. I understand well that this is confusing

the inla-output in the result object is not clear on this point, which
is a consequence of the output not being 'designed' for suchs. the
holde'output' should be redesigned at some point...

anyway, here is how

if the model X is replicated Y times, then the output is

c(X.rep1, X.rep2, ..., X.repY)

I added a small test which demonstrate this

the issue gets more involved if the model is also 'grouped' by
introducing some dependence and then replicated. then the storage is

X.group1.rep1, X.group2.rep1, ...., X.groupG.rep1, X.group1.rep2, ....


the function

inla.idx

defines this, and can compute the index where each element is found.
like

> inla.idx(3, n=10,replicate=3, nrep=3, group=1,ngroup=1)
[1] 23


so with three replicates and no group (ie ngroup=1), then the index for
x[3] at replicate 3, is 23.


hope this helps,
H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] getting replicate information
parts:
Dear all,

I understand how the ID's are generated and that they are ordered by Y. My current workaround is below. However it will only work as long as the assumption on their order remains valid. I'm willing to attempt to patch this in the rinla code if someone can point me the files that needed to be updated.

library(dplyr)
r$summary.random$idx %>%
  mutate_(
    Replicate = ~rep(
      seq_len(n() / n_distinct(ID)),
      each = n_distinct(ID)
    )
  )

Best regards,

Thierry
